cards.source: Cairns, Hass-Klau & Goodwin, 'Traffic Impact of Highway Capacity Reductions: Assessment of the Evidence' (Landor, 1998)
cards.claim: When road capacity is removed, part of the traffic does not reappear elsewhere ('traffic evaporation'), but the share varies widely from case to case.

cards.source: Evaluations of the 2016 closure of the Voie Georges-Pompidou (Paris right-bank lower quays)
cards.claim: After the lower quays closed, monitoring reported traffic shifting onto nearby parallel routes, including the upper quays, alongside a debate about how much traffic evaporated.

cards.source: Evaluations of London Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (e.g. Goodman et al., 2021)
cards.claim: The effect of filtering streets on surrounding roads differs from site to site, so displacement onto other streets has to be checked locally rather than assumed away.
Residential streets have a limited 'environmental capacity': beyond a certain traffic level, living conditions degrade even if the street can physically carry more vehicles.
